faqs.question: What does BCR ABL1 Mutation Analysis measure?
faqs.answer: BCR ABL1 Mutation Analysis detects genetic mutations in the BCR ABL1 fusion gene, specifically for CML.

faqs.question: Why is BCR ABL1 Mutation Analysis done?
faqs.answer: • To identify genetic mutations in the BCR ABL1 gene for patients with CML • To guide treatment decisions by determining therapy resistance markers • To monitor treatment effectiveness and assess the need for changes in therapy • To provide valuable information for personalized treatment plans

faqs.question: When is BCR ABL1 Mutation Analysis recommended and who should take the test?
faqs.answer: BCR ABL1 Mutation Analysis is recommended for • patients diagnosed with CML, • patients with suspected therapy resistance or treatment failure, • patients whose treatment response needs to be monitored, and • patients requiring personalised treatment plans based on genetic information.

faqs.question: What if the results of the BCR ABL1 Mutation Analysis are abnormal?
faqs.answer: The presence of BCR ABL1 gene mutations may indicate therapy resistance in CML. Abnormal results help doctors identify appropriate treatment options.

faqs.question: What to expect during the BCR ABL1 Mutation Analysis?
faqs.answer: During this test, a sample of 5–10 ml of EDTA whole blood will be collected. The sample is sent for analysis using Sanger Sequencing.

faqs.question: What preparations are required before the BCR ABL1 Mutation Analysis?
faqs.answer: • Clinical diagnosis, test prescription, and TRF are mandatory. • Follow any instructions provided by your doctor regarding medication or dietary restrictions. • Inform your doctor if you have any specific requirements.

faqs.question: What other tests may be ordered with BCR ABL1 Mutation Analysis?
faqs.answer: • Complete Blood Count (CBC): To assess the overall blood cell counts and morphology • BCR ABL1 Quantitative PCR: To monitor treatment response and measure disease burden • Bone Marrow Aspiration and Biopsy: To evaluate the extent of bone marrow involvement

faqs.question: What is the BCR ABL1 Mutation Analysis also known as?
faqs.answer: Genetic Testing for Therapy Resistance in Chronic Myeloid Leukaemia

faqs.question: What is chronic myeloid leukaemia?
faqs.answer: Chronic myeloid leukaemia is a type of cancer that affects the white blood cells. It is characterised by the overproduction of abnormal white blood cells in the bone marrow. CML is often associated with a genetic abnormality known as the Philadelphia chromosome.

faqs.question: What is the BCR ABL1 Mutation Analysis Test?
faqs.answer: The BCR ABL1 Mutation Analysis Test is a genetic test that detects mutations in the BCR-ABL1 fusion gene, specifically in the ABL1 kinase domain. It helps identify resistance to tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) in patients with certain types of leukaemia.

faqs.question: Is home sample collection available for the BCR ABL1 Mutation Analysis Test?
faqs.answer: Yes, some labs, including Metropolis, offer home sample collection for the BCR-ABL1 Mutation Analysis Test in which a trained phlebotomist will visit your home to collect the required blood samples, maintaining the highest standards of sample handling and testing accuracy.

faqs.question: What are the normal levels for BCR ABL1 Mutation Analysis Test?
faqs.answer: Normal levels in the BCR ABL1 Mutation Analysis Test indicate no detectable mutations and BCR-ABL1 transcript levels below a specific threshold, such as <0.1% IS for CML patients on TKIs.

faqs.question: What is a BCR ABL1 Mutation Analysis Test used for?
faqs.answer: The BCR ABL1 Mutation Analysis Test is used to identify mutations that confer resistance to TKIs, monitor disease response, and guide treatment adjustments in patients with CML and Ph+ ALL.

faqs.question: How often should I get tested for a BCR ABL1 Mutation Analysis Test?
faqs.answer: The frequency of the BCR ABL1 Mutation Analysis Test depends on your clinical response and treatment protocol. Typically, it is performed every 3-6 months or as clinically indicated by your doctor.

faqs.question: What time should I get the BCR ABL1 Mutation Analysis Test done?
faqs.answer: You can get the BCR ABL1 Mutation Analysis Test done at any time, following your doctor's recommended schedule.

faqs.question: Is fasting required for the BCR ABL1 Mutation Analysis Test?
faqs.answer: No, fasting is not required for the BCR ABL1 Mutation Analysis Test.

faqs.question: Are there any other precautions to be taken before getting myself tested for a BCR ABL1 Mutation Analysis Test?
faqs.answer: Ensure that your sample is handled and transported correctly to the laboratory.

faqs.question: What parameters are included in the BCR ABL1 Mutation Analysis Test?
faqs.answer: The BCR ABL1 Mutation Analysis Test includes sequencing of the ABL1 kinase domain and quantification of BCR-ABL1 transcripts.

faqs.question: When should the BCR ABL1 Mutation Analysis Test be done?
faqs.answer: The BCR ABL1 Mutation Analysis Test should be done when there are signs of resistance to TKIs, loss of haematologic or cytogenetic response, or disease progression. It is also part of regular monitoring for patients with CML or Ph+ ALL, as recommended by your doctor.

faqs.question: How much time does the BCR ABL1 Mutation Analysis Test take?
faqs.answer: Sample collection for the BCR ABL1 Mutation Analysis Test takes a few minutes, but laboratory processing takes several days.

faqs.question: How soon can I get the reports for the BCR ABL1 Mutation Analysis Test?
faqs.answer: Reports for the BCR ABL1 Mutation Analysis Test are typically available within 10 days after the laboratory receives your sample based on the day/time when the sample was collected and processed. The turnaround time may vary depending on the complexity of the analysis required.
